page: UpCloud GPU-24xCPU-240GB-1xB200 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8570 processor running at 2.0 GHz, providing 24 physical cores and 24 vCPUs with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, yielding 10.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware component is the single NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPU, which provides 192 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across memory and specialized instruction sets. The instance achieved a passmark CPU score of 52754.5 and a passmark CPU extended instructions test score of 67506.68, supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions). Memory bandwidth is strong, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4156.98 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 115.78 GB/sec. In LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M model, the server achieved top-tier results with 9953.26 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 525.92 tokens/sec for text generation.

The shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent architectural tradeoffs that require external storage solutions and may introduce resource contention. However, the high density of VRAM relative to the 24 vCPUs makes it a resource-dense option for GPU-heavy tasks. This server is suited for workloads such as large language model inference, machine learning training, data science jobs, and cryptographic operations.
